It just doesn't reach for the newer Astro 5+/7 affordances (astro:env schema, stable route caching) that would have replaced a little hand-rolled code.

The one gap is skipping AbortController for the debounced search, leaving stale requests running to completion where the platform offers cancellation.

app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:82-99 — humanize/format helpers hand-written in ~30 lines rather than pulling lodash/classnames-style packages

dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: two deps, both current stable, and everything the platform or a 30-line helper can cover was written in-house. Nothing to trim.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:1-99 + app/src/lib/data.ts:1-250 — all API access, URL building and caching centralized behind two modules; a PokeAPI shape change is contained here (good)

app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:22-34, moves/[name].astro:23-26, abilities/[name].astro:20-23, types/[name].astro:14-17, 404.astro:3 — the try/catch NotFoundError → Astro.response.status=404 block is copy-pasted into five files; the sixth resource page would copy it again
app/tsconfig.json:3-4 — strict: false and allowJs: true, actively undoing astro/tsconfigs/base's strict default

app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:37,99 — getJson/getList return Promise<any>; the measured 8 type lines mean API responses flow through the whole app untyped, so an upstream shape change fails silently at render time
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:18-180 — ~160-line frontmatter mixes fetching, aggregation and view-shaping for the most complex page
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, config and URL construction are properly centralized, and no framework internals or undocumented behavior are touched. But types at boundaries are essentially absent (strict off, `any` everywhere) and the not-found boilerplate is duplicated across every route, so both API changes and framework upgrades ripple further than they should.

findings.issue: Every API response is typed `any` (getJson, getList, and all consumers), and tsconfig sets strict: false, so there is no boundary between the external PokeAPI shape and the app.
findings.suggestion: Turn strict back on (the astro/tsconfigs/base default) and define interfaces for the resources actually consumed (NamedAPIResource, Pokemon, Species, Move, Type…) in lib, returning them from getJson/getList instead of `any`.

findings.issue: The try/catch NotFoundError → status-404 block is duplicated verbatim across moves, abilities, types and pokemon pages (plus 404.astro), so adding or changing a resource page means copying the pattern a fifth/sixth time.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared helper such as loadResourceOrNotFound(fn), or centralize not-found handling in Astro 7's advanced-routing src/fetch.ts (which gained a notFound() handler in 7.4).

findings.issue: Debounced search uses a manual requestId counter; in-flight fetches are never cancelled, only ignored on arrival, so rapid typing still completes every request server-side.
findings.suggestion: Create an AbortController per navigation and call abort() when a newer one starts — the platform-native way to cancel, which also relieves the server.

findings.issue: API_BASE_URL is read via process.env with an inline default, so the variable is untyped and unvalidated.
findings.suggestion: Declare it in the astro:env schema (envField.string({ context: 'server', access: 'public', optional: true, default: ... })) and import from astro:env/server for type safety and build-time validation.

findings.issue: A bespoke promise-memoization cache is layered over every fetch, duplicating concern the framework now covers (Astro 7 stabilized route caching via `cache`/`routeRules` with memoryCache()).
findings.suggestion: The data-layer cache is defensible given the 'live API' requirement and query-keyed pages, but consider Astro 7's stable route cache (maxAge/swr) for the mostly-static routes (types, abilities) to shrink custom code.

findings.issue: Versions are exact-pinned (7.4.4 / 11.1.9) with no range, so patch and security releases require a manual bump each time.
findings.suggestion: Use caret ranges (^7.4.4 / ^11.1.9) as Astro's own scaffolding does, relying on the lockfile for reproducibility.

findings.issue: server: { host: true } configures the dev/preview server; in standalone mode the adapter documents HOST/PORT env vars at runtime instead.
findings.suggestion: Harmless but unneeded for production serving — drop it or confirm it is only there for dev convenience.

summary: This is a current-generation Astro 7 app: the right adapter mode, the right output mode, two dependencies, and no legacy APIs to be found. Data access and caching are cleanly centralized behind two lib modules, which is where most future churn would otherwise live. The forward-looking weaknesses are the total absence of typed boundaries (strict off, `any` from every fetch) and a not-found pattern copy-pasted into five files, plus a couple of missed modern affordances (astro:env, AbortController, Astro 7's stable route caching).

apis.replacement: astro:env schema (envField) — supported but astro:env is the newer type-safe recommendation
